reports.published_report: Kaelen Culpepper is a power-forward shortstop who's translating above-average contact skills into consistent impact—.273/.377/.498 at AAA with an .875 OPS built on 88th-percentile ISO shows a bat that plays. The main risk is contact consistency; he'll need to sustain that hit tool as he moves up, since strikeout creep is common in translation to the majors. The 289-PA sample is current and substantial, and ValuCast's projection leans everyday regular with low risk, which aligns with the on-field production to date.

reports.name: Kyson Witherspoon
reports.peak_summary: Projection: back end starter with medium risk. The current pitching shape is starter volume over 51 IP.
reports.published_report: Kyson Witherspoon is a 21-year-old right-hander working in A+ whose stuff generates strikeouts but whose command profile lags behind the swing-and-miss. He's punching out 9.5 K/9 while walking 4.8 BB/9, yielding a 5.12 ERA and 1.45 WHIP across 51 innings—all pedestrian in percentile rank when measured against the pitcher pool (K/9 at 47th, BB/9 at 47th, K-BB% at 48th). The core problem is that walk rate; even the MLB-equivalent translation shows a projected 4.5 BB/9, well above the 3.2 big-league average, suggesting control is the floor that keeps him from a more optimistic ceiling. With only 51 innings in hand at a single level, the skill picture is still emerging, but current command issues are real.
reports.report: There's no repeatable way to retire hitters in the line yet; the failure point is the strikeout-to-walk result, which does not support a firm starter projection. A rotation role is not supported by the current line; the floor is organizational depth or a low-leverage bullpen assignment. The sample covers 51 IP in High-A, so confidence is low.

reports.name: Owen Murphy
reports.peak_summary: Projection: back end starter with medium risk. The current pitching shape is mixed over 48.7 IP.
reports.published_report: Owen Murphy is a righthander showing solid control and chase rates at AAA, but his strikeout production lags the upper tier—9.8 K/9 in the minors translates to just 8.8 K/9 in an MLB context, below league average. His walk rate climbs to 4.2 BB/9 when adjusted for level, a meaningful tick above the 3.2 MLB average and the primary drag on his 12.8% K-BB%. The risk is straightforward: he'll need swing-and-miss gains or continued refinement in pitch execution to stay ahead of hitters at the next level, rather than rely on contact management alone. The 69-inning sample is fresh and sufficient.
reports.report: A rotation role is not supported by the current line; the floor is organizational depth or a low-leverage bullpen assignment; there's no repeatable way to retire hitters in the line yet. Neither misses nor strikes separate in the strikeout-to-walk result; the sample covers 48.7 IP in Triple-A, so confidence is high.
